## Extraction safety: every consumer of the budget cluster (moved out of the description, P4 cap)

The budget cluster (`_WORKFLOW_TOKEN_BUDGET_BYTES`, `_payload_bytes`,
`_cap_workflow_payload`) moves from `mcp_server.py` to `src/rebar/_mcp_budget.py`. The
plan-review gate correctly blocked an earlier revision for claiming "nothing else in the
server calls them" while scoping that check to `mcp_server.py` alone. The full consumer set,
enumerated by grepping the symbol names across the repo:

**Inside `mcp_server.py`** — the definitions themselves, plus
`cap_workflow_payload=_cap_workflow_payload` on the shared tool context (`:636`).

**Outside `mcp_server.py`, referencing the symbol on its namespace — these would break on a
bare move:**

| consumer | reference |
|---|---|
| `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py:98` | `cap_workflow_payload=ms._cap_workflow_payload` |
| `tests/unit/test_gen_mcp_reference.py:122` | `cap_workflow_payload=ms._cap_workflow_payload` |
| `tests/interfaces/facades/test_workflow_mcp_schema.py:36,43,67` | `from rebar.mcp_server import _cap_workflow_payload` |

**Through the tool context, not the namespace — unaffected either way:**
`_mcp_reads.py:250` binds `_cap_workflow_payload = ctx.cap_workflow_payload`, used at `:598`
and `:612` for `get_workflow_status` / `get_workflow_result`.

**Resolution: RE-EXPORT, not repoint.** `mcp_server.py` imports `_cap_workflow_payload`,
`_bound_list_payload` and `_LIST_TOKEN_BUDGET_BYTES` back into its own namespace, so all three
external consumers keep working **unedited** and `rebar.mcp_server._cap_workflow_payload`
stays a valid import path. Repointing them at `rebar._mcp_budget` was the alternative; it was
rejected because it enlarges the change for no benefit and breaks any out-of-tree caller using
the same path. The three files passing unedited is the evidence that the re-export holds.

## Auth precondition for live validation — corrected

An earlier revision described the deployed endpoint as behind "the OAuth gate". That is wrong:
`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STRATEGIES=static`, i.e. per-client **static bearer PATs**
(`MCP_CLIENT_PAT_COPILOT` / `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX` / `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLAUDE`, see
`docs/mcp-client-setup.md:25-27`), not an OAuth authorization-code flow. The contract is
unchanged — a valid bearer token is required and a `401`/`403` is a FAILED validation, not an
environment excuse — only the mechanism is named correctly.
